'''''Nights of Ryscate and Diamonds''''' was the famous last work of the celebrated [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] author [[Custo Ramak]], written on his [[Death/Legends|deathbed]]. The [[Book/Legends|book]] was a deeply sentimental autobiographical account of his hedonistic and luxurious lifestyle in [[Coronet City/Legends|Coronet City]], the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]. Published well before the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], ''Nights of [[Ryshcate/Legends|Ryscate]] and [[Diamond/Legends|Diamonds]]'' became particularly famous after Ramak's death, and over the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] hundreds of young [[Artist/Legends|artists]] were drawn to Coronet City in search of the fortune and fame described within.<ref name="Codex" />

==Behind the scenes==
''Nights of Ryscate and Diamonds'' was first mentioned in the Codex entry for Coronet City in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', a [[Star Wars video games|video game]] released by [[BioWare]] and [[LucasArts]] in [[2011]]. The work's name is a misspelled reference<ref name="Codex" /> to [[Ryshcate/Legends|ryshcate]], a Corellian [[Foodstuff/Legends|pastry]] used to mark special occasions.<ref name="Rogue">''[[X-Wing: Rogue Squadron]]''</ref>
